PC: Appropriately treat the patient with naloxone
Recognize the progressive dyspnea after the naloxone administration
Attempt to oxygenate and ventilate the patient using either a non-rebreather oxygen mask or NIPPV.
Recognize that the patient’s O2% saturation is not improving by any means, and perform rapid sequence intubation or awake intubation.
Establish lung-protective ventilator settings (e.g., tidal volumes 6-8 mL/kg or even as low as 4-6 mL/kg; rate 14-18; FiO2 100% initially; plateau pressure <30 mmH2O; PEEP 5 mmH2O initially)11
MK: Recognize that the patient is unresponsive due to opioid overdose
Reassess the patient and diagnose pulmonary edema
Recognize that oxygenation is still poor despite maximizing ventilator settings
SBP: Initiate advanced ICU management (e.g., prone positioning, advanced ventilator modes, neuromuscular blockage), ECMO procedures per local protocol, or consider transfer to a higher level of care8
